title: Object
spec: Start by creating a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees for all axes and a translation vector of (0.0, 0.0, 0.0233) to position the origin slightly above the default plane. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on the first face. In this sketch, create a single circle with its center at (0.0233, 0.0233) and a radius of 0.0233. After drawing the circle, apply a scaling factor of 0.0465 to the entire sketch to adjust its size accordingly. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into a three-dimensional object by rotating it according to the Euler angles and translating it using the previously defined vector. Finally, extrude the transformed sketch along its normal by 0.6977 units to create a solid cylindrical body. The final dimensions of the object will be a length of 0.04651162790697674, a width of 0.04651162790697674, and a height of 0.6976744186046512.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the sketch
sketch = (
    cq.Workplane("XY")
    .moveTo(0.0233, 0.0233)
    .circle(0.0233)
)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylinder
cylinder = sketch.extrude(0.6977, both=False)

# Translate the cylinder to the desired position
cylinder = cylinder.translate((0.0, 0.0, 0.0233))

# Assign the final model to 'r'
r = cylinder

import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial coordinate system
workplane = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the sketch for the base of the cylinder
sketch = (
    workplane
    .center(0.0233, 0.0233)  # Move to the center of the circle
    .circle(0.0233)  # Draw a circle with the given radius
)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylinder
cylinder = sketch.extrude(0.6977)

# Scale the sketch (if necessary)
# Note: The sketch scale is applied to the sketch before extrusion, but in this case, it's 0.0466 which is the diameter of the circle.
#       Since the circle is already defined with the correct radius, scaling is not necessary here.

# Final model
r = cylinder
